title: Payment Tracker App – frontend naming + delivery export package + publish-flow docs

requirements.summary: Rename all user-facing strings to consistently use the production name “Payment Tracker App” across the frontend UI and docs.
acceptanceCriteria: Browser tab title shows "Payment Tracker App" (instead of "Monthly Payment Tracker").
Login screen title/branding uses "Payment Tracker App" (instead of "Monthly Payment Tracker").
App header brand label uses "Payment Tracker App" (instead of "Payment Tracker").
No remaining user-visible occurrences of "Finance Tracker" in the frontend README or UI copy.

file_operations.description: Update the document <title> to “Payment Tracker App” and ensure any other visible metadata strings do not reference prior names.
Update login screen branding text to “Payment Tracker App”, including the app icon alt text and the large title string (replace “Monthly Payment Tracker”).
Update the in-app header brand label to “Payment Tracker App” and ensure header icon alt text is appropriate and consistent with the new app name.
Update README title and any occurrences of “Finance Tracker” / older app naming to “Payment Tracker App”, ensuring user-visible documentation matches production branding.

requirements.summary: Add a repo-local delivery export package containing a project structure snapshot and a reproducible regeneration script/command.
acceptanceCriteria: A new top-level delivery folder exists containing an index file that lists the full project folder structure.
Delivery folder includes documented steps to regenerate the export from the repository (single command or clearly ordered steps).
The export content includes both backend and frontend code folders in the structure listing.

file_operations.description: Create a human-readable project structure index (tree listing) that explicitly includes both frontend/ and backend/ in the listing (as repo paths), suitable for delivery packaging.
Document how to regenerate the delivery snapshot from the repository sources (single command or clearly ordered steps), including how to re-create the structure listing and problem-files collection.

Add a reproducible script that regenerates the delivery snapshot (structure listing + copies/refreshes problem-files) directly from the repo sources without manual copying; keep it runnable from repo root or with clearly documented working directory expectations.

requirements.summary: Collect build/deploy troubleshooting “problem files” into a dedicated subfolder under the delivery package with a README describing relevance.
acceptanceCriteria: A dedicated subfolder exists under the delivery folder (e.g., delivery/problem-files/) containing the selected build/deploy-related config/docs files.
A README in that subfolder lists each included file and its troubleshooting relevance (e.g., env examples, type env declarations, build/deploy docs).

file_operations.description: Create a short README that enumerates each collected file and explains how it helps diagnose build/deploy failures (environment configuration, frontend build setup, IC/II configuration, etc.).
Include a copy of frontend/.env.example (renamed for clarity in the delivery folder) to aid troubleshooting environment-variable-related build and runtime configuration.
Include a copy of frontend/src/vite-env.d.ts to aid troubleshooting TypeScript env typing issues that can break builds.
Include a copy of frontend/index.html to aid troubleshooting asset paths, metadata/title, and entrypoint configuration that can affect builds/deploys.
Include a copy of frontend/README.md to aid troubleshooting by providing the documented local build/run steps and prerequisites used for deployments.

requirements.summary: Stabilize the publish flow by documenting a deterministic frontend build/deploy procedure and adding troubleshooting notes aligned with what was fixed.
acceptanceCriteria: A full build and deploy can be executed end-to-end without intermittent failures caused by missing configuration, type errors, or dependency issues.
A short deployment troubleshooting note is added to documentation (or delivery notes) describing what was fixed and how to reproduce a successful deploy.

file_operations.description: Add a concise deployment/build troubleshooting section focused on deterministic frontend steps (install/build), required tooling versions, and common failure causes (missing env vars, type errors, dependency install state), including how to reproduce a successful build.
Add delivery notes describing what was fixed/standardized to prevent intermittent publish failures and a reproducible checklist to validate a successful frontend build prior to deployment.
Link the delivery regeneration steps to the deployment troubleshooting notes and ensure the delivery package explains how the included snapshots/problem-files support diagnosing publish issues.
